---
name: omnifocus-workflow
description: Shared conventions, bucket mapping, and tag system for the OmniFocus skill family. Read this before running any OmniFocus skill.
---

# OmniFocus Workflow with Cowork

This doc is the shared context the OmniFocus skills need to behave like Mark expects. The skill files themselves focus on *how to call the MCP*; this doc captures *Mark's conventions*.

**Skills that read this:** `omnifocus-capture`, `omnifocus-query`, `omnifocus-inbox-triage`, `omnifocus-focus`.

Mark drives weekly / project reviews directly in the OmniFocus app, not through a skill. The cadence data below is reference only.

---

## 1. The Three Buckets

Mark organizes work into three buckets. These map cleanly onto existing OmniFocus folders.

| Bucket | Folders | Projects |
|---|---|---|
| **Personal/Family** | Family, Me, Learner and Explorer | Household, Husband, Father, Me, Friendship, Important Reading Queue, Photography, Experiments |
| **APR** (Agile Pain Relief) | APR Business Owner | Initiatives (folder: per-outcome projects), Operations, Ideas & Reading, Marketing Experiments |
| **YFL** (Your Financial Launchpad) | YFL CTO | YFL Other |

**Notes:**
- Personal/Family spans three folders but is one bucket for routing purposes.
- YFL is early-stage (only one project at time of writing). Expect this to grow.
- When a skill talks about "bucket," it means one of these three. Use folder membership to determine bucket.

### Bucket routing notes (confirmed 2026-04-19)

- **Programming was removed 2026-04-20.** Contents migrated to Experiments. Project status = dropped (kept for history). Do not route anything to Programming.
- **Experiments is the broad catch-all** in the Learner and Explorer folder. It absorbs: actual software development work, automation, tool tweaks, Obsidian setup and customization, Keyboard Maestro / Alfred / iOS Shortcuts tweaks, dashboard building, tool-of-the-week experiments, PKM methodology trials.
- **"Learner and Experimentation" is Mark's shorthand for the Experiments project.** Treat the phrase as a direct reference to that project, not the folder.
- **Important Reading Queue (Me):** dual-purpose. May contain both personal and business-oriented reading. Route to the project when named, never assume bucket.
- **Reading vs. practicing a technique:** if the task is "read about X," it goes to Important Reading Queue. If the task is "try X in my own life or work," it usually belongs in Experiments (personal) or the relevant APR project (business).
- **YFL:** this is Mark's wife's business. Low volume. Unlikely to need sub-folders soon. Keep the one-folder pattern.

### APR mode-based structure (added 2026-05-31)

APR Business Owner is organised by **mode**, not subject area. Four buckets:

- **Initiatives** (folder, one project per outcome) — committed multi-step work with real dependencies. Examples currently active: `GenAI Cohort Launch`, `Drip → Cakemail Cleanup`, `Vendor & Tool Migrations`, `A-CSM Relaunch`. When Mark says "I'm starting X" or commits to a launch, capture as a new project here. Drop the project when the outcome ships.
- **Operations** (single-actions, weekly review) — recurring admin and meta-tasks: bills, licence renewals, weekly analytics pull, monthly GSC export, bi-weekly blog refresh, etc. Anything that repeats on a cadence lives here.
- **Ideas & Reading** (single-actions, monthly review) — parking lot for curiosities, reading material, "consider X," "look into Y." Tagged by theme: `AI Exploration`, `Business Strategy`, `Tooling Curiosity`. Monthly review = scan, prune, promote 1-2 to Initiatives if Mark commits.
- **Marketing Experiments** (single-actions, weekly review) — one task per active experiment; see the Marketing Experiments pattern section below.

**Replaces the old subject-area projects** (Business Evolution, Ongoing Business, Website, Pragmatic LLM Uses, Agile and AI) which were all dropped 2026-05-31. The old names became fuzzy idea-queues rather than coherent projects, which made review mechanical.

**Routing rule for APR captures:**
- Committed multi-step outcome? → Initiatives (existing project, or new one if it's a new commitment — ask)
- Recurring admin or maintenance? → Operations
- Curiosity, idea, reading item? → Ideas & Reading (with the right theme tag)
- Marketing test with a measurement window? → Marketing Experiments (one new task; see below)
- If unclear, ask. Don't infer.

### Routing patterns observed (from 2026-04-19 triage; APR rows updated 2026-05-31)

These patterns emerged from the first batch triage session. Use them as defaults, not rigid rules. Always confirm when uncertain.

| Capture shape | Usual destination |
|---|---|
| Obsidian plugin, dashboard, or vault setup tweak | Experiments |
| Alfred, Keyboard Maestro, iOS Shortcuts automation | Experiments |
| "Check out this new tool / app / workflow" (personal curiosity) | Experiments |
| Claude / MCP integration research for business use | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` |
| AI tool Mark wants to evaluate for business use | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` (or `Tooling Curiosity` if tooling-for-tooling) |
| YFL application work (Supabase, etc.) | YFL Other |
| Business file/vendor cleanup (recurring) | Operations (APR) |
| Business migration off a vendor (committed) | Initiatives > Vendor & Tool Migrations (APR) — or new Initiative project if scope warrants |
| Personal file/systems cleanup | Me |
| GenAI experiments tied to Scrum / Agile (idea or reading) | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` |
| GenAI cohort launch work | Initiatives > GenAI Cohort Launch (APR) |
| Course prep / delivery / ops (recurring) | Operations (APR) |
| Course relaunch (committed initiative) | Initiatives > new project, e.g. A-CSM Relaunch (APR) |
| APR marketing content / keynote ideas | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `Business Strategy` (or `AI Exploration` if AI-focused) |
| APR strategic question or "should I X?" | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `Business Strategy` |
| Drip → Cakemail migration cleanup | Initiatives > Drip → Cakemail Cleanup (APR) |
| Recurring APR admin (bills, licence renewals, analytics pulls) | Operations (APR) |
| Marketing experiment (new test) | Marketing Experiments (APR) — one new task with vault note |
| Writing/glossary idea | `APR/TaskNotes/` in the vault (not OmniFocus). One file per idea, frontmatter: `tags: task`, `status: LongTerm`, `priority: normal`, `ContentType: [Blog \| Glossary \| Newsletter]`. Filename = the idea title. Body optional (URLs, context). Mark moves them to `APR/Efforts/Glossary/` or `APR/Efforts/Blog/` manually when the work begins. |
| Reading material (book, article, paper) | Important Reading Queue |
| Physical shopping or household purchases | Household |
| Camera or photography gear | Photography |
| Self-development practice (techniques to try in daily life) | Me or Experiments |
| Coaching / questioning techniques | Experiments (as practice material) |

**Mark's colloquial project names vs. where they now go (updated 2026-05-31):**

| Mark says | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| "APR Business" | Depends on shape — recurring admin → Operations; strategic idea/question → Ideas & Reading (Business Strategy tag); committed launch → Initiatives (new or existing project). Ask which. |
| "Learner and Experimentation" | Experiments (personal, Learner and Explorer folder) |
| "Agile AI" / "Agile and AI" | Ideas & Reading + AI Exploration tag; or GenAI Cohort Launch if it's clearly cohort work |
| "Pragmatic LLM usage" | Ideas & Reading + AI Exploration tag |
| "Marketing experiment" / "new experiment" | Marketing Experiments — one new task with rich note + vault link |
| "I'm starting [X]" / "new initiative" | New project in Initiatives folder |
| "Business Evolution" / "Ongoing Business" / "Website" / "Pragmatic LLM Uses" | These projects were dropped 2026-05-31. Route by mode (see above) instead. |

### Marketing Experiments pattern (APR) — restructured 2026-06-16

Marketing Experiments are tracked in two linked places:

- **Vault note per experiment** in `APR/Analytics/Experiments/` — holds the Goal, Baseline, What Changed, Result, Learning narrative. Index at `APR/Analytics/Experiments/_Experiments Index.md`.
- **One parent task per experiment** inside the single `Marketing Experiments` project under `APR Business Owner` (project type = single-actions list, weekly review). The parent name + note carry just enough context to act; the vault note holds the depth.

**Why this shape (not project-per-experiment):** experiments aren't multi-step projects — they're "make a change, wait, check results." A project wrapper per experiment caused review blur (near-identical mini-projects all looking the same in review). One parent task per experiment keeps the whole portfolio visible at a glance.

**The Do → Measure structure (added 2026-06-16):** an experiment has two phases that must not be conflated — *doing the work* and *measuring the result later*. Each parent task is **sequential** with exactly two subtasks:

- **`Execute: <action>`** — the change/work. Pull-based, no due date.
- **`Measure: <metric>`** — blocked until Execute is complete. **Set its due date only when Execute is checked off**, at the measurement window (below). This is the mechanism that stops "remember to go get the data" from quietly evaporating once the work is done.

When the work was finished before this structure existed, create the Execute subtask already-completed and set the Measure due date immediately.

**Measurement window defaults (SEO/content experiments):**

- **Linking or refresh of existing pages → ~8 weeks** after the work ships (re-crawl + re-rank of pages Google already knows).
- **New posts / pillar pages → ~12 weeks** (new URLs need indexation time before they accrue enough impressions to read).
- In practice, measure at the **next monthly GSC refresh on or after** that mark. Non-SEO experiments (newsletter, lead-magnet) use the window named in their own vault note.

**Task conventions:**

- **Parent name:** experiment name without the date suffix, e.g. `Question-Format Subject Lines`.
- **Parent note:** one line of context (goal / next action), then a blank line, then the `obsidian://open?vault=MarkPKM&file=...` link to the vault note (URL-encode spaces as `%20`, slashes as `%2F`). Keep the depth in the vault note, not here.
- **No due date on the parent or the Execute subtask.** Only the Measure subtask carries a due date, and only once Execute is done.
- **No tags by default.** Flag the parent at review time if the experiment is the focus of the week (`Weekly Plan` tag is the equivalent signal).

**Weekly review mechanism:** during Sunday review, open the `Marketing Experiments` project and **flag 1-2 parents** to surface them for the week. Measure subtasks with a due date surface on their own.

**Completion:** when the Measure subtask is done, mark the parent complete and update the vault note's `Result` and `Learning` sections.

**Triggering:** when Mark says "new marketing experiment [name]", capture a **new parent task** (with the Execute → Measure subtasks) in the `Marketing Experiments` project — not a new project, not a new folder — and ask whether the vault note already exists or needs to be created.

### Triage-specific rules learned

- **Already-done items:** during triage, Mark sometimes reveals an inbox item is already complete. Mark it completed (`completed: true`) instead of moving it. Easier than a move-then-complete.
- **Ghost inbox items:** the inbox will contain some items with `status: dropped` that never fully cleared. Flag them to Mark but leave them alone. Cleanup happens in the OmniFocus app.
- **Tags during triage:** Mark occasionally tags at triage time (for example, `Weekly Plan` on items that belong in a weekly planning view). Triage skill supports `add_tags` per item, use it.
- **"Skip" means leave in inbox.** Don't drop, don't defer, just leave the item where it is so Mark can handle it manually.

---

## 2. Capture Conventions

- **Default destination: inbox.** Always, unless Mark explicitly names a project in the ask.
- Example triggers that still go to inbox: "add a task to call Sam", "drop this in OmniFocus"
- Example trigger that goes to a project: "add 'refactor login flow' to Website"
- Single captures proceed without confirmation.
- Batch captures (more than one task) get a confirmation step.
- Never infer a project from context. If Mark's wording is ambiguous, ask.

---

## 3. Roles and the Status-Tag Pull System (restructured 2026-06-14)

Mark runs a roles-pull system adapted from MacSparky's Roles workshop. Roles set the "what am I working on" axis; status tags set the Kanban lane. Tasks are "endeavours" in that language. This replaces the old flat planning/state tag scheme (the previous Bench / Consider Next / Quarterly Plan setup).

### Roles = folders

The three in-scope roles map one to one onto OmniFocus folders. Folder membership *is* the role, so there are no role tags.

| Role | Folder |
|---|---|
| Learner and Explorer | Learner and Explorer |
| APR Business Owner | APR Business Owner |
| YFL CTO | YFL CTO |

Family and Me are parked (not yet rolled in). Arete statements for each role live in [Self/Roles.md](../Self/Roles.md). They are the values filter for deciding what is worth pulling onto a given week.

### Status tags (the Kanban lanes)

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *(untagged)* | **Idea / backlog.** The default. Anything without a status tag is an idea, not a commitment. |
| `Shelf` | Warm queue. On-deck, coming back soon. |
| `Next Week` | Committed for next week. The staging lane. |
| `Weekly Plan` | Committed for this week. The week's pool. |
| `Doing` | In progress right now. The active lane, and where the tight WIP limit lives. |
| `Waiting` | Blocked on someone else. A separate axis, not part of the pull flow. |

No `Done` tag. Completing the task in OmniFocus *is* done. Add one only if a draggable "done" board column is ever wanted.

### The pull flow

Backlog (untagged) to `Shelf` to `Next Week` to `Weekly Plan` to `Doing` to completed.

- **WIP limits.** The tight, meaningful limit lives on `Doing`, the active lane (start around 1 to 3). `Weekly Plan` carries a looser weekly commitment cap (around 5 to 7). Both apply only to discretionary endeavour work; Mark sets the numbers.
- **Pull into `Doing` as you start.** Day to day, move an item from `Weekly Plan` to `Doing` when you actually begin it, and out again when you stop or complete it. `Doing` is the honest "what am I touching right now" lane.
- **Recurring Operations tasks carry no status tag.** Analytics pulls, GSC export, blog refresh, and the like flow on their own recurrence plus due dates and never count against the WIP limit. They are maintenance throughput, not pulled endeavours.
- **Mid-week arrivals destined for next week get `Next Week`, never `Weekly Plan`.** This keeps the current week's board stable once it is set; the item joins this week only when Sunday promotes it.
- `Weekly Plan` is the canonical "this week" signal across all folders. Where the Marketing Experiments pattern (Section 1) says "flag to surface for the week," the `Weekly Plan` tag is the equivalent; flagging stays a compatible secondary highlight.

### The Sunday pull (weekly review event, done in the OmniFocus app)

1. Complete or clear what finished.
2. Promote `Next Week` into `Weekly Plan`.
3. Refill `Next Week` and `Shelf` from the backlog, up to the WIP limit.
4. Glance at the role mix: is any role starving?

The review is the forcing function. It is what keeps the backlog from breeding zombies (the old `Quarterly Plan` problem): quarter candidates simply sit as backlog or `Shelf` and get pulled forward when they are actually due, instead of wearing a sticky tag that never expires.

### Tag migration (applied 2026-06-14; supersedes the 2026-04-19 cleanup plan)

Done in OmniFocus on 2026-06-14:

- **Added:** `Shelf`, `Next Week`.
- **Kept:** `Weekly Plan` (now the WIP lane), `Waiting` (unchanged: blocked on someone else).
- **Folded into `Shelf`:** the 11 live tasks carrying `Consider Next` were re-tagged to `Shelf`; `Bench` had no tasks. Both tags set to `dropped`. `Bench` is retired because its old meaning ("paused") is the opposite of MacSparky's bench ("active this week").
- **Retired quarter tags:** `Quarterly Plan` and `Q2 2026` set to `dropped` and stripped from their 13 live tasks (which fall back to untagged backlog); the older quarter tags (`Q1`-`Q4 2025`, `Q3`/`Q4 2024`) were already dropped.
- Dropped tags are hidden, not hard-deleted, so they are recoverable; hard-delete in the app if wanted.
- 8 tasks in dropped/dead projects still carry the now-hidden old tags; left untouched per the ghost-item rule.

### Other existing tags (unchanged by this change)

- **Ideas & Reading themes:** `AI Exploration`, `Business Strategy`, `Tooling Curiosity`. Tag tasks inside the `Ideas & Reading` project (APR) to filter the parking lot by theme during monthly review.
- **GTD contexts:** `Phone Calls`, `Errands`, `Home`, `Office`, `Online`, `Communications`.
- **Recurrence cadence:** `Daily`, `Weekly`, `Monthly`, `Quarterly`, `SemiAnnually`, `Annually`.
- **Domain / utility:** `Health`, `Writing`, `Glossary`, `Checklist`, `Automate`. People / scope: `Family`, `Friends`. (The old `Heatlh` typo is already fixed.)
- **Leftover:** the `!Plan` grouping tag is still active but unused by this scheme; retire it whenever convenient.

---

## 4. Review Cadence (observed)

Pulled from project `reviewIntervalValue` / `reviewIntervalUnit` on 2026-04-19:

| Project | Folder | Interval |
|---|---|---|
| Me | Me | Every 4 days |
| Household | Family | Every 2 weeks |
| Husband | Family | Every 9 days |
| Father | Family | Every 23 days |
| Friendship | Me | Every 10 days |
| Important Reading Queue | Me | Weekly |
| Photography | Learner and Explorer | Every 2 weeks |
| Experiments | Learner and Explorer | Every 16 days |
| GenAI Cohort Launch | APR > Initiatives | Weekly |
| Drip → Cakemail Cleanup | APR > Initiatives | Every 2 weeks |
| Vendor & Tool Migrations | APR > Initiatives | Monthly |
| A-CSM Relaunch | APR > Initiatives | Every 2 weeks |
| Operations | APR | Weekly |
| Ideas & Reading | APR | Monthly |
| Marketing Experiments | APR | Weekly |
| YFL Other | YFL CTO | Every 23 days |

**Cadence pattern:** APR Initiatives + Operations + Marketing Experiments review weekly to bi-weekly; Ideas & Reading reviews monthly (it's a parking lot, not a commitment list). Personal/Family varies. Old subject-area APR projects (Business Evolution, Website, Ongoing Business, Pragmatic LLM Uses, Agile and AI, Ship30For30) all dropped 2026-05-31 in the mode-based restructure.

**Review is done in the OmniFocus app**, not via a skill. Skills may surface review-adjacent info when asked (e.g. "what's stalled") via `omnifocus-query`.

---

## 5. Focus / Perspective Use

### Confirmed 2026-04-19

- Mark uses two custom perspectives: **Weekly Plan** and **Quarterly Plan**. Both are general (not bucket-specific) and rarely used.
- **Focus is a nice-to-have, not a daily habit yet.** The `omnifocus-focus` skill ships minimal: set focus on a bucket folder, clear focus, show current focus. No perspective switching wired in yet.
- **Bucket to folder mapping for focus:**
    - "Focus on APR" → set focus on `APR Business Owner` folder
    - "Focus on YFL" → set focus on `YFL CTO` folder
    - "Focus on Personal/Family" → spans three folders (`Family`, `Me`, `Learner and Explorer`). The skill should ask which specific folder, or apply all three if the MCP supports multi-folder focus.
    - "Clear focus" → reset

Revisit perspective integration once Mark actually starts using focus regularly.

### Kanban status board (added 2026-06-14)

The status tags from Section 3 (`Shelf`, `Next Week`, `Weekly Plan`, `Doing`) are designed to drive a custom perspective grouped by tag. That grouping is the Kanban board, one column per lane. Filter it to a single folder for a one-role board, or leave it across all three folders for the whole picture. OmniFocus 4 has no native board view, so tag-grouping is the approximation. Repoint the existing "Weekly Plan" perspective at this scheme; the "Quarterly Plan" perspective can be retired along with the quarter tags.

---

## 6. Recurrence (repeating tasks and projects)

The MCP supports recurrence on both tasks and projects. Use `create_tasks` / `create_projects` to seed the task, then apply recurrence via `update_tasks` / `update_projects` (the create calls don't take recurrence fields directly as of 2026-04-20).

### Fields

- `recurrence` — an iCalendar RRULE string, or `""` to clear recurrence.
- `repetition_method` — how the next occurrence is scheduled:
    - `fixed` — next occurrence is calculated from the *original* schedule, regardless of when it's completed. Best for rhythms that should happen on a consistent day (weekly review, monthly bills).
    - `start_after_completion` — next defer date is X after you actually complete it. Best for tasks where the gap between completions matters more than the date (water the plants, lubricate the bike chain).
    - `due_after_completion` — next due date is X after you actually complete it. Similar to above but for due-dated tasks.

### Common RRULEs

| Cadence | RRULE |
|---|---|
| Every day | `FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=1` |
| Every weekday | `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR` |
| Weekly | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1` |
| Every 2 weeks | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2` |
| Monthly | `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=1` |
| Quarterly | `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=3` |
| Annually | `FREQ=YEARLY;INTERVAL=1` |

### Default choices

- **Rhythms (weekly review, analytics pull, reviews)** → `repetition_method: fixed` so the cadence stays consistent.
- **Maintenance tasks (chores, bike tune-up, HVAC filter)** → `repetition_method: start_after_completion` so the clock resets on completion.
- **Due-dated tasks (bill pay, quarterly filing)** → `repetition_method: due_after_completion`.

### Reading recurrence from a task

The `get_tasks` response includes `isRecurring`, `recurrence` (RRULE), `repetitionMethod`, and `repeatSummary` (human-readable, always prefer this for display). `nextDueDate` / `nextDeferDate` are populated for recurring tasks.

### Safe update pattern

```python
update_tasks(tasks=[{
    "id": task_id,
    "recurrence": "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1",
    "repetition_method": "fixed"
}])
```

Clearing recurrence: `recurrence: ""`.

---

## 7. Skill Safety Rails (applies to all)

- **Reads:** no confirmation needed.
- **Single writes** (one task create, one task update): proceed immediately, report result.
- **Batch writes** (more than one task affected): show the plan, wait for approval.
- **Deletes:** always confirm. Prefer `drop` over `delete` unless Mark says "permanently delete."
- **Recurring task completion:** use the MCP's proper completion mechanism, never a raw "set completed to true" pattern. The MCP handles next-occurrence generation.

---

## 8. Cowork Bridge Notes

- The OmniFocus MCP runs on Mark's Mac. From Cowork, the `mcp__omnifocus__*` tools call into it directly.
- If the MCP is disconnected, the skills can't run. Tell Mark to restart Claude Desktop / re-enable the MCP.
- Rich data is available via MCP; no need for pasted output or dump files.

---

*Last updated: 2026-06-16 (Marketing Experiments Do → Measure subtask structure + measurement-window defaults; Section 1). Update this doc whenever conventions change. The skills read it at runtime to stay aligned.*

# Social Media Posting Workflow

Reference for how APR social/LinkedIn content gets drafted, where past topics live, and what decides which blog posts go into the next round. The moving parts live in the `agile-pain-relief-astro` and `social-media-posting` repos, not the vault.

## 1. Skills for drafting LinkedIn posts

There is no dedicated "give me a topic, get a post" drafting skill in the vault. The pieces that exist:

- **`apr-linkedin-style`** (`Skills/apr-linkedin-style.md`) reviews/critiques an existing draft against Mark's voice and LinkedIn conventions (length, hooks, emoji, hashtags, links). It does not generate or rewrite posts wholesale.
- **`evergreen-posting`** (Astro repo: `.claude/skills/evergreen-posting/SKILL.md`) is the actual batch generator. Give it "N days" of content and it drafts three-platform posts (LinkedIn / Mastodon / Bluesky) promoting evergreen content, then writes a JSON file the pipeline consumes.
- **`social-media-adapt`** (Astro repo) converts a single LinkedIn post to Mastodon/Bluesky format.
- **`criticmarkup-editing`** delivers voice critiques as inline suggestions when the draft is a Markdown file.
- `storybrand-messaging` / `Marketing/copy-editing` if the post leans promotional.

Realistic flow: `evergreen-posting` (or hand-draft) → `apr-linkedin-style` voice check → adapt/schedule.

## 2. Where past drafted topics live

- **Vault drafts:** `APR/Efforts/Social Media/` (filenames ending `-drafts` by convention). Currently `next-few-days-drafts.md` and `Surviving the AI Tsunami - Social Ideas.md`.
- **Pipeline batch JSON:** `agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/` (written by `evergreen-posting`; the pipeline drains and refills `next-few-days.json`).
- **Posted history / prior promo language:** `analytics/history.json`, `history-archive.json`, `old_history.json` in the Astro repo. Grep a slug to find how a piece was promoted before, then mirror that angle/hashtags.

## 3. What decides which blog posts go into the next round

Governed by the **`evergreen-posting`** skill's "Content selection" rules, drawing from a curated queue:

- **Source of truth for blog posts:** `agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/complete-social-media-calendar.md`, specifically its **"Posting Queue"** section.
  - Skip anything marked `[x]` (already promoted).
  - Work the tiers in order: **TIER 1** (GenAI / supports the webinar) → **TIER 2** (proven traffic drivers) → **TIER 3** (Scrum & leadership staples).
- **Quiz hooks:** `social-media/planning/AI Failure Modes Quiz Generated Posts.md` (skip blocks marked `[POSTED YYYY-MM-DD]`).
- **Default cadence:** 3 posts/weekday = 2 quiz + 1 blog/glossary, interleaved so a day isn't all one theme.
- **Queue hygiene:** `npm run calendar-audit` (in `social-media-posting`) diffs the reshare queue against the live blog/glossary so it doesn't drift from what's actually published.

Short version: the **Posting Queue in `complete-social-media-calendar.md`** decides *which* blog posts are eligible and in what priority; the **`evergreen-posting` skill** applies the tier/skip rules to pick the next round.

## Key paths

- Astro repo: `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro`
- Posting pipeline repo: `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/social-media-posting`
- Shared authoring conventions: `agile-pain-relief-astro/.claude/skills/_social-posting-conventions.md`

Found the mismatch. Here's what's going on and how to fix it properly.

## Where the two numbers actually live

- **The real cadence (source of truth):** `buffer-post/slotAllocator.ts` → `DEFAULT_SLOT_PLAN` = `[{10:00}, {13:30}]`. That's **2 posts/weekday**. This is what the scheduler actually does.
- **The header's claim:** `calendar-audit/calendarAudit.mjs:93` hardcodes the string `**Cadence:** 3 posts/weekday (2 quiz + 1 calendar item)`, and line 34 hardcodes `const ITEMS_PER_WEEK = 5` (which drives the runway calc).

So the header is a **hand-typed string in the audit script**, not derived from the posting code. `npm run calendar-audit --write` faithfully rewrites that same wrong "3/weekday" every time. The audit syncs the queue counts against the live site, but it never syncs the cadence line against the scheduler.

## Why it drifted

At 2 slots/day, "3 posts/weekday (2 quiz + 1 calendar)" is impossible. The honest description at 2/day is **1 quiz + 1 calendar item per day**. Note that still drains ~5 calendar items/week, so `ITEMS_PER_WEEK = 5` and the runway are actually still fine. Only the cadence sentence is wrong.

## How to keep them in sync

The clean fix is to make the audit **derive the posts/weekday number from the slot plan** instead of typing it:

1. **Extract the slot plan into a shared module** both sides import, e.g. `buffer-post/slotPlan.mjs` (plain JS/JSON) that `slotAllocator.ts` re-exports and `calendarAudit.mjs` imports. One definition, two consumers.
2. In `buildHeader`, print `${SLOT_PLAN.length} posts/weekday` instead of the literal `3`. Now the header can never disagree with the scheduler.
3. The **quiz-vs-calendar split and `ITEMS_PER_WEEK` can't come from the slot times** (the code doesn't know a slot is quiz vs calendar), so those stay as an explicit, commented constant. Set the mix line to match reality: `1 quiz + 1 calendar`.

The one thing to accept: slot *count* is code-derivable and should be; the *content mix* is an evergreen-posting authoring decision and has to be stated, not inferred.

Two ways I can do this:
- **Quick correctness patch:** just fix the two lines in `calendarAudit.mjs` to say "2 posts/weekday (1 quiz + 1 calendar)". Fast, but it'll drift again if you ever change the slot plan.
- **Durable sync:** the shared-module refactor above, so the cadence auto-tracks `DEFAULT_SLOT_PLAN`.

Want me to do the durable version? It's a small refactor (one new file, two edits), and it makes the code genuinely the source of truth.

Make the **posting code the single source of truth** for the "posts/weekday" cadence shown in the header of
`agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/complete-social-media-calendar.md`, so the header can never
drift from what the scheduler actually does. Mark will handle this refactor separately; this doc is the brief.

## The problem (already diagnosed)

- Real cadence lives in `social-media-posting/buffer-post/slotAllocator.ts` → `DEFAULT_SLOT_PLAN`
  = `[{hour:10,minute:0}, {hour:13,minute:30}]` = **2 posts/weekday**. This is what the scheduler does.
- The calendar header's cadence line is a **hardcoded string** in
  `social-media-posting/calendar-audit/calendarAudit.mjs`:
  - Line ~34: `const ITEMS_PER_WEEK = 5;`
  - Line ~93 (inside `buildHeader`): `` `**Cadence:** 3 posts/weekday (2 quiz + 1 calendar item); ...` ``
  - Line ~94: runway line, computed from `ITEMS_PER_WEEK`.
- Result: `npm run calendar-audit --write` keeps rewriting "3 posts/weekday", which contradicts the 2-slot
  scheduler. The audit syncs queue counts vs the live site, but never syncs cadence vs the scheduler.
- Current header (in the calendar file) wrongly reads: `**Cadence:** 3 posts/weekday (2 quiz + 1 calendar item)`.

## The chosen fix: durable sync

1. **Extract the slot plan into a shared, plain-JS module** both consumers import, e.g.
   `social-media-posting/buffer-post/slotPlan.mjs` (or `.json`). It holds the single `DEFAULT_SLOT_PLAN`
   definition.
   - `slotAllocator.ts` re-exports it (keep its existing `SlotPlan` interface / `DEFAULT_SLOT_PLAN` export
     surface intact so nothing downstream breaks; the `.ts` just imports the values from the shared module).
   - `calendarAudit.mjs` imports it too.
   - Note the `.mjs` (audit) vs `.ts` (allocator) split: a plain `.mjs`/`.json` shared module is importable by
     both without a build step. Verify the TS side still typechecks / tests pass.
2. **Derive the number in the header** — in `buildHeader`, print `${SLOT_PLAN.length} posts/weekday`
   instead of the literal `3`. Now cadence auto-tracks the slot plan.
3. **Content mix + `ITEMS_PER_WEEK` are NOT code-derivable** (the slot times don't know quiz vs calendar).

   which still drains ~5 calendar items/week, so `ITEMS_PER_WEEK = 5` and the runway math stay valid.
   Update the mix wording in the header string from "(2 quiz + 1 calendar item)" to "(1 quiz + 1 calendar item)".

=== blog frontmatter sample ===
---
title: "GenAI Code Quality – The Fundamental Flaws and How Bluffing Makes It Worse"
date: "2026-02-12"
lastUpdated: '2026-02-12'
categories:
  - "artificial-intelligence"
  - "agile-engineering-practices"
coverImage: '@/content/blog/genai-code-quality-fundamental-flaws-and-how-bluffing-makes-it-worse/images/genai-code-quality-four-flaws-training-maintainability-security-codebase.png'
excerpt: 'AI-generated code has 1.7x more issues and the flaws are structural, not fixable by code review. Why training rewards bluffing over quality, and what to do about it'
---
import Figure from '@/components/global/figure.astro';
import CalloutBox from '@/components/global/callout-box.astro';
import GenAICodeQualityImg from '@/content/blog/genai-code-quality-fundamental-flaws-and-how-bluffing-makes-it-worse/images/genai-code-quality-four-flaws-training-maintainability-security-codebase.png';

AI-generated code has 1.7x more issues, the GenAI code quality gap is turning into a chasm. That's not a random number, that's from a CodeRabbit research report[^1]. You've probably already seen the problem yourself. AI-generated, quick to write, harder to read and maintain. Why? Researchers from the GENIUS project[^3] put it plainly: training focuses on pass/fail — does the code compile, does it pass the tests? There's no reward for writing code that's easy to maintain.
=== glossary frontmatter sample ===
src/content/glossary/10-minute-build/
---
title: '10 Minute Build'
date: '2022-09-28'
lastUpdated: '2025-05-01'
relatedTerms: ['agile-engineering-practices', 'continuous-integration']
excerpt: When builds are slow, Developers wander off to do new things'
---

import HighlightBox from '@/components/global/highlight-box.astro';

**10 Minute Build** is the idea that we should be able to build a system and run its test suites in 10 minutes or less. Fast build-and-test provides quicker feedback to the developers who wrote the code. It allows them to move on to the next thing - a new feature or improving the current one. Fast builds allow for multiple check-ins per person/pair a day, which in turn makes small check-ins practical. These smaller check-ins reduce the risk of team members stepping on each other's virtual toes and, with a bit of practice, allow them to develop a rhythm that results in continuous small improvements.

Fast builds are a stepping stone for Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery.

In comparison, when builds are slow, Developers wander off to do new things while waiting (See: Multitasking), which results in increased cost to go back and fix defects when they're found later in the build, especially since longer builds are run less often so it will take longer to find errors.

content.text:
Confirmed, the key signal is there: `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv` tags reshare-driven visits with `utm_campaign=archive-reshare`, so you can see sessions-per-page-per-platform directly (e.g. Human Cost of GenAI pulled 29 Mastodon sessions on 2026-07-12). That's the backbone of a major update.

## Minor update (what we just did)

**Cadence: monthly**, plus opportunistically when you publish something you'll want to reshare soon.

- It's cheap: `npm run calendar-audit --verbose` surfaces "live but not in the queue," and the recent-by-date filter I ran picks out the new stuff.
- Best home: a recurring **Operations** task, ideally piggybacked on your monthly GSC export so it's one sitting.
- Rule of thumb: if you published 1-2 posts this month, just add them; the full audit is only worth it monthly.

## Major update (performance re-tier)

**Cadence: quarterly.** Reshare performance needs a quarter to accumulate signal, and re-tiering is a judgment call, not a mechanical merge. Natural home: fold it into your **quarterly review**.

The process, all from data you already collect:

1. **Refresh the data.** Run `apr-weekly-analytics` (scrapes social metrics into `history.json`, runs `posthog-export`). Then `apr-content-performance` for the synthesized snapshot.
2. **Read three "is it working?" signals, in priority order for a reshare queue:**
   - **Social to site clicks per page** (the direct one): `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv`, filtered to `archive-reshare`, summed per page per platform. This is literally "which queued pieces earn clicks when reshared."
   - **Social engagement per post**: `history.json` engagement (reactions, comments, impressions, engagementRate). Tells you which *angles/hooks* land, separate from click-through.
   - **Evergreen traffic value** (secondary): `export-pageviews-by-week-utm-source-and-pathname.csv` + Ahrefs top pages. Catches SEO-strong pages worth reshares even if social is quiet.
3. **Re-tier the queue:**
   - Promote consistent reshare performers into **TIER 2** (they earn periodic reshare).
   - Demote or retire pieces that got multiple reshares and near-zero clicks to the bottom, or cut them.
   - Keep fresh GenAI in **TIER 1** regardless of numbers (it's strategic, supports the webinar).
   - Pull in any high-traffic page that isn't in the queue at all.
4. **Refresh the header** with `calendar-audit --write`.

The one judgment trap: don't over-index on raw sessions. A piece with 29 Mastodon clicks might just be recency (it was posted that week). Normalize by number of times reshared, and weight LinkedIn (your main audience) over Mastodon/Bluesky.

## Worth noting

`apr-content-performance` is the analysis engine, but **turning its output into a re-tiered queue isn't codified anywhere yet**. Right now that's manual. Want me to build a small skill (say, `apr-reshare-queue-tune`) that runs the quarterly major update end to end: pull the reshare attribution, rank the queue's posted items by clicks-per-reshare, and propose tier moves for your approval? That would make the major update repeatable instead of a from-scratch analysis each quarter.

---
name: apr-reshare-queue-tune
description: Quarterly performance re-tier of the social-media reshare queue. Checks the queue's already-posted items against PostHog reshare attribution and social engagement to see what's actually working, then proposes tier moves (promote / demote / retire) and pulls in high-traffic pages that aren't queued. Use when Mark says "tune the reshare queue", "re-tier the calendar", "which reshares are working", or runs the quarterly social-media queue review.
triggers:
  - tune the reshare queue
  - re-tier the calendar
  - which reshares are working
  - reshare queue review
  - quarterly social queue update
---

# APR Reshare Queue Tune (quarterly major update)

Re-prioritise the reshare queue in `complete-social-media-calendar.md` based on what actually drives clicks and engagement, not gut feel. This is the **major** update. The **minor** update (curating recently published posts/glossary into the queue) is a separate monthly job (see "Minor vs major" below) and does not need this skill.

Run this **quarterly**, ideally folded into the quarterly review.

## Distinction: minor vs major

- **Minor (monthly):** add newly published blog posts and glossary entries to the queue. Just `calendar-audit --verbose` + curate the recent-by-date items into the right tier. No performance data needed.
- **Major (quarterly, this skill):** look at the queue's *posted* items, measure how each performed when reshared, and move items between tiers. Data-driven, needs an approval gate.

## Paths (read-only from the Astro repo)

- Queue file (the thing being re-tiered, in the Astro repo): `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/complete-social-media-calendar.md`
- Reshare attribution: `.../analytics/posthog/export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv` (filter `utm_campaign=archive-reshare`)
- Overall page traffic: `.../analytics/posthog/export-pageviews-by-week-utm-source-and-pathname.csv`
- Social engagement per post: `.../analytics/history.json`
- SEO top pages (secondary): `.../analytics/Ahrefs/`
- Audit + header refresh tool: `social-media-posting` repo, run `npm run calendar-audit` from the **Astro repo root**.

## Procedure

### 1. Refresh the data first

Run `apr-weekly-analytics` (scrapes social metrics into `history.json`, runs `posthog-export`). If that was run in the last few days, skip. Optionally run `apr-content-performance` for the synthesized snapshot as background context.

### 2. Build the reshare-performance table

For every **posted** (`[x]`) item in the queue, compute:

- **Reshare clicks (LinkedIn-weighted):** from `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv`, rows where `utm_campaign=archive-reshare`, grouped by `entry_path` and `utm_source`, `sessions` summed.
  - **Overlap caveat:** these are rolling 30-day snapshots appended by `snapshot_date`. Summing every row double-counts overlapping days. Dedupe to the **latest snapshot per (entry_path, utm_source)**, or use snapshots spaced ~30 days apart. State which you used.
  - Weight LinkedIn highest (main audience), then Mastodon, then Bluesky. A simple weighting: `LinkedIn*1.0 + Mastodon*0.4 + Bluesky*0.3` (adjust with Mark).
- **Times reshared:** count occurrences of the slug in `history.json` (and honour the `(…, Nx)` markers already in the queue). Compute **clicks per reshare** = weighted clicks / times reshared. This is the primary ranking signal — it normalises out "posted more recently / more often."
- **Engagement:** average `engagement.linkedin.engagementRate` (and reactions+comments) across that URL's posts in `history.json`. Secondary signal — measures whether the hook lands even if click-through is low.

A node one-liner over the CSV + JSON is the fastest way to assemble this; write it inline, don't hand-count.

### 3. Rank and classify

- **Top performers** (high clicks-per-reshare) not already in TIER 1/2 → propose **promote to TIER 2** (Proven Traffic Drivers).
- **Duds** (multiple reshares, near-zero clicks *and* weak engagement) → propose **demote to the bottom of their tier**, or **retire** (comment out / move to a "Rested" list — do not hard-delete unless Mark says so).
- **TIER 1 GenAI stays TIER 1** regardless of numbers — it's strategic and supports the webinar. Flag underperformers for a hook rewrite instead of demotion.
- **Not-yet-queued high-traffic pages:** scan `export-pageviews-by-week-...csv` + Ahrefs top pages for pages pulling real traffic that aren't in the queue at all → propose adding them (usually TIER 2).

### 4. Guard against false signals

- **Recency bias:** a piece reshared last week will show clicks purely from recency. Always divide by times-reshared; don't rank on raw sessions.
- **Small numbers:** ignore differences below a handful of sessions; call out low-confidence rows rather than acting on them.
- **Platform mix:** a Mastodon-only spike is weaker evidence than steady LinkedIn clicks.

### 5. Present, then apply (approval gate)

- Present the ranked table and the proposed tier moves **in chat for approval** — this is a batch edit to an existing file, so it always confirms first (per Mark's rules).
- On approval, edit `complete-social-media-calendar.md`: move the `- [ ]` / `[x]` lines between tier sections, keeping the posted markers intact.
- Then run `npm run calendar-audit --write` from the Astro repo root to refresh the header counts.
- Leave the changes unstaged for Mark's normal commit flow unless he says otherwise.

## Output

# APR Reshare Queue Tune (quarterly major update)

Re-prioritise the reshare queue in `complete-social-media-calendar.md` based on what actually drives clicks and engagement, not gut feel. This is the **major** update. The **minor** update (curating recently published posts/glossary into the queue) is a separate monthly job (see "Minor vs major" below) and does not need this skill.

Run this **quarterly**, ideally folded into the quarterly review.

## Distinction: minor vs major

- **Minor (monthly):** add newly published blog posts and glossary entries to the queue. Just `calendar-audit --verbose` + curate the recent-by-date items into the right tier. No performance data needed.
- **Major (quarterly, this skill):** look at the queue's *posted* items, measure how each performed when reshared, and move items between tiers. Data-driven, needs an approval gate.

## Paths (read-only from the Astro repo)

- Queue file (the thing being re-tiered, in the Astro repo): `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro/social-media/planning/complete-social-media-calendar.md`
- Reshare attribution: `.../analytics/posthog/export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv` (filter `utm_campaign=archive-reshare`)
- Overall page traffic: `.../analytics/posthog/export-pageviews-by-week-utm-source-and-pathname.csv`
- Social engagement per post: `.../analytics/history.json`
- SEO top pages (secondary): `.../analytics/Ahrefs/`
- Audit + header refresh tool: `social-media-posting` repo, run `npm run calendar-audit` from the **Astro repo root**.

## Procedure

### 1. Refresh the data first

Run `apr-weekly-analytics` (scrapes social metrics into `history.json`, runs `posthog-export`). If that was run in the last few days, skip. Optionally run `apr-content-performance` for the synthesized snapshot as background context.

### 2. Build the reshare-performance table

For every **posted** (`[x]`) item in the queue, compute:

- **Reshare clicks (LinkedIn-weighted):** from `export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv`, rows where `utm_campaign=archive-reshare`, grouped by `entry_path` and `utm_source`, `sessions` summed.
  - **Overlap caveat:** these are rolling 30-day snapshots appended by `snapshot_date`. Summing every row double-counts overlapping days. Dedupe to the **latest snapshot per (entry_path, utm_source)**, or use snapshots spaced ~30 days apart. State which you used.
  - Weight LinkedIn highest (main audience), then Mastodon, then Bluesky. A simple weighting: `LinkedIn*1.0 + Mastodon*0.4 + Bluesky*0.3` (adjust with Mark).
- **Times reshared:** count occurrences of the slug in `history.json` (and honour the `(…, Nx)` markers already in the queue). Compute **clicks per reshare** = weighted clicks / times reshared. This is the primary ranking signal — it normalises out "posted more recently / more often."
- **Engagement:** average `engagement.linkedin.engagementRate` (and reactions+comments) across that URL's posts in `history.json`. Secondary signal — measures whether the hook lands even if click-through is low.

A node one-liner over the CSV + JSON is the fastest way to assemble this; write it inline, don't hand-count.

### 3. Rank and classify

- **Top performers** (high clicks-per-reshare) not already in TIER 1/2 → propose **promote to TIER 2** (Proven Traffic Drivers).
- **Duds** (multiple reshares, near-zero clicks *and* weak engagement) → propose **demote to the bottom of their tier**, or **retire** (comment out / move to a "Rested" list — do not hard-delete unless Mark says so).
- **TIER 1 GenAI stays TIER 1** regardless of numbers — it's strategic and supports the webinar. Flag underperformers for a hook rewrite instead of demotion.
- **Not-yet-queued high-traffic pages:** scan `export-pageviews-by-week-...csv` + Ahrefs top pages for pages pulling real traffic that aren't in the queue at all → propose adding them (usually TIER 2).

### 4. Guard against false signals

- **Recency bias:** a piece reshared last week will show clicks purely from recency. Always divide by times-reshared; don't rank on raw sessions.
- **Small numbers:** ignore differences below a handful of sessions; call out low-confidence rows rather than acting on them.
- **Platform mix:** a Mastodon-only spike is weaker evidence than steady LinkedIn clicks.

### 5. Present, then apply (approval gate)

- Present the ranked table and the proposed tier moves **in chat for approval** — this is a batch edit to an existing file, so it always confirms first (per Mark's rules).
- On approval, edit `complete-social-media-calendar.md`: move the `- [ ]` / `[x]` lines between tier sections, keeping the posted markers intact.
- Then run `npm run calendar-audit --write` from the Astro repo root to refresh the header counts.
- Leave the changes unstaged for Mark's normal commit flow unless he says otherwise.

Adds recently published content the queue is missing. Cheap, low-judgement.

### Copy-paste prompt

```
Update the social media reshare queue with recently published content.

1. cd to /Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro
2. Run `npm run calendar-audit -- --verbose` to see what's live but not in the queue.
3. Find blog posts and glossary entries published since the last time I curated
   (check publish dates from the `date:` frontmatter field; sort newest first).

   - High-search proven traffic pages -> TIER 2

5. After I approve, add them as unposted `- [ ]` lines in the right sections,
   then run `npm run calendar-audit -- --write` to refresh the header counts.
```

### Notes

- The `date:` frontmatter is the publish date; `lastUpdated:` is a refresh and should be ignored for "recently published."
- New items go in as `- [ ]` (unposted). The `(YYYY-MM-DD)` suffix is only for posted `[x]` items.

Re-tiers the queue based on performance. Uses the `apr-reshare-queue-tune` skill. Do the data refresh first (or confirm this week's Monday pull already ran).

```
Run the quarterly reshare queue tune (apr-reshare-queue-tune skill).

1. Make sure the data is fresh: if apr-weekly-analytics hasn't run in the last few
   days, run it (scrapes social metrics into history.json, runs posthog-export).

   - Reshare clicks from analytics/posthog/export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv,
     rows where utm_campaign=archive-reshare, grouped by entry_path + utm_source.
     Dedupe to the latest snapshot per page/source (the snapshots overlap - don't
     sum every row). Weight LinkedIn 1.0, Mastodon 0.4, Bluesky 0.3.
   - Times reshared: count the slug across history.json (+ the "(…, Nx)" markers).
   - Clicks-per-reshare = weighted clicks / times reshared (primary ranking signal).
   - Engagement: average engagementRate + reactions/comments from history.json.
3. Rank and propose tier moves:
   - Top performers not in TIER 1/2 -> promote to TIER 2.
   - Duds (many reshares, near-zero clicks AND weak engagement) -> demote to bottom
     of tier, or retire to a "Rested" list (don't hard-delete).
   - Keep TIER 1 GenAI in TIER 1 regardless; flag weak ones for a hook rewrite.
   - Scan pageviews CSV + Ahrefs top pages for high-traffic pages NOT in the queue
     and propose adding them.
4. Guard against false signals: divide by times-reshared (kill recency bias), ignore

5. Show me the ranked table + proposed moves and WAIT for approval (batch edit).
6. After I approve, edit complete-social-media-calendar.md (move the lines between
   tiers, keep posted markers), then run `npm run calendar-audit -- --write`.
```

- Rank on **clicks-per-reshare**, never raw sessions (raw sessions just reward whatever was posted most recently / most often).
- LinkedIn is the main audience; a Mastodon-only bump is weak evidence.
- The full method lives in the skill: `Skills/apr-reshare-queue-tune.md`.
- Leave the edits unstaged for your normal commit flow.

---

- Reshare attribution: `agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/posthog/export-entry-path-by-utm-source.csv`
- Social engagement: `agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/history.json`
- Audit tool: `npm run calendar-audit` (run from the Astro repo root)
